decisions.reason: Captures 가뜩이나 with “already” and renders 달갑지 않은 상황 in plainer English than BASE’s formal “hardly a welcome development.”
BASE drops 놈들; SOL drops 면상. Keep both the bastards and the faces.
decisions.replacement: *Let’s see what these bastards’ faces look like.*

decisions.reason: “Immediately spotted” matches 발견한 without BASE’s “eyes fell on” body-part calque.
Comma on the parenthetical estimate is standard; “as if” vs “as though” is no gain.
SOL’s “everyone knew everyone” is unsupported; 고만고만한 is the village being small and unremarkable.
“A merchant he recognized” matches 익숙한 얼굴의 more precisely than “a familiar merchant.”
“Going by age” captures 따지면; SOL’s “could be” weakens the 애비지 boast.
decisions.replacement: “Going by age, I’d be his father.”

decisions.reason: 관군 should stay “government troops,” matching the rest of the chapter.
Same 관군 echo; “troops” keeps the chapter term consistent.
Identifies 관복을 차려입은 현령 directly instead of delaying through “a man…the county magistrate.”
“Even put on” carries 관복까지; BASE’s “too” underplays 까지.
탄성 is admiring exclamations, not an “uproar.”
Cavalry 달려오는 toward a welcome is galloping, not charging; “turned to follow everyone’s gaze” is cleaner than “turned his head in the direction of.”
“Even he” supplies the 이었지만 / 이름만은 contrast BASE leaves implicit.
“Maintained its lineage” keeps 명맥을 이어 온; SOL flattens that to mere age.
SOL drops 만 (“alone”); the point is that even the visible Jin martial artists numbered dozens.
SOL collapses 낭중지추, the pouch-awl simile, and 이상한 일도 아니다; BASE keeps all three beats.
“Filled me with pride” is the more natural 뿌듯하다 rendering.
BASE’s “just like that thing” is stiff; SOL overspecifies “chant” and turns the period-separated lines into shouts.
decisions.replacement: This was that thing, wasn’t it? *Milky-skinned Jin Taekyung. We love you, Jin Taekyung.*

decisions.reason: Korean marks [이름 없는 검] in running prose; dropping the item brackets is an unsupported convention change.
BASE keeps the 전체 이용가 all-audiences rating joke; SOL’s “beloved” is not in the Korean.
Glossary requires 귀환자 as Returnee; System field capitalization is consistent with the other labels.
Splitting the former +10/+100 effect into its own sentence is clearer than “changed from.”
Korean states a general 명성/칭호 rule; BASE’s “one’s” is stiff, SOL’s “my Fame” narrows it.
decisions.replacement: It seemed that a Title’s effect increased as Fame rose.

decisions.reason: 크으으 is a savoring groan, not a giggle; “Now that’s the stuff” hits that beat. 주모 here is the tavern call, not the household-mistress glossary sense.
“To my right” places Hyuk Mujin more clearly than “on my right.”
사람들이 좋아하니까 is the crowd enjoying the scene, not “people like me.”
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
말고삐를 당겨 means they were mounted; BASE’s “Walking” contradicts the reins.
쏟아져 나와 is pouring out; SOL’s “poured into” drops the coming-out.
Accepts merging the speech tag into the following line.
Tag plus question in one line is natural English and keeps 어리둥절해져서 물었다.
Accepts merging Hyuk Mujin’s whisper tag into the following line.
Same whisper-plus-speech merge; the name is preserved, not dropped.
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
SOL’s “around here” is more spoken, but “arrest” flattens 잡아가는; keep the hauling-off.
decisions.replacement: Violent crimes happened dozens of times a day around here, yet I had never once seen government troops drag away a criminal.

decisions.reason: 때려잡는 is beating/cracking down, not generic “deal with.”
SOL drops 헛기침을 했다 from the narration and the unmotivated past perfect is worse.
“Of some standing” is the idiomatic 나름 직위가 있는; “with a certain position” is translationese.
적당히 대처한 is a passable excuse, not a “convenient” one; 그제야 still needs “finally.”
decisions.replacement: I’d only offered a reasonable excuse, but the county magistrate’s expression finally relaxed a little.

decisions.reason: “Endured great hardship” fits the magistrate’s register for 노고가 크셨을 텐데 better than “gone through.”
Simple past “remained” is the natural sequence; BASE’s extra past perfect is heavy.
얘기해 주려던 is telling him, not explaining.
Shocked spoken English for 오백 명이 넘는 마적단; “mounted-bandit force” is stiffer with no extra meaning.
Comma makes the magistrate’s echo of 너무 read as a question instead of a pileup.
너무 축소됐네요 is the number being too reduced; “far too low” tracks that better than “understatement.”
Drops an extra “And” the Korean does not have; 심지어 still lands on “even.”
벌레 보는 is looking at a bug; SOL’s “reserved for a bug” reads as if the face belongs to one.
하늘을 우러러 is facing/looking up to heaven; “beneath the heavens” is a different image.
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
“Watch your expression” is the spoken 표정 관리; “manage your expression” is calqued.
처리한 is “took care of,” not specifically “kills”; “become Master” is also cleaner than “make Master.”
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
Keep 우러러 as “before the heavens”; “verbal footwork” is the 혀 드리블, and “completely win over” keeps 마음을 쏙 빼놓았다.
decisions.replacement: Hyuk Mujin, who had lived a truthful life without a single shameful moment before the heavens, used dazzling verbal footwork to completely win over the county magistrate.

decisions.reason: 입에서 나오는 말 is words coming out of his mouth; SOL’s “comes from” genericizes it.
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
허어어어어 is an elongated gasp; SOL’s “Good heavens” sanitizes the comic sound.
Replaces six-dot …… with the required ellipsis character.
Short exclamation matches 지랄이 풍작이다 as a punchline; BASE’s “At this point, this was” is padded.
“As if” and “as though” for 것처럼 are interchangeable.
After the magistrate admits he got carried away, past “did you have” asks after the original 볼일.
소가주님 말이오 puts the clarification after the title, matching “The Lesser Family Head, I mean.”
술에 떡이 돼서 말이지 is the because-explanation for why they are hidden; SOL drops that causal link.
“So much as” carries 표정 하나 변하지 않고.
것 같습니다 needs “I don’t think”; SOL’s “to interrupt” spells out an implication the Korean leaves trailing.
decisions.replacement: “I’m sorry, but he’s currently circulating his qi, so I don’t think he can see you. As you know, County Magistrate, it’s quite dangerous.”

decisions.reason: 는지 … 마련하셨소 is one causal thought; BASE’s “so he arranged” keeps that link without SOL’s choppy split.
